method: Actual first-author per-word linguistic pass now completed by reading all 392 exact word/gloss/tag applications against the already curated 100 source-bound templates, then validating source equality, explicit root/clitic, imperative or infinitive, object number/gender and command person/number. Independent of Spec detailed decisions; no native-human certification.
chronology: Source-bound template curation and mechanically filtered research applications came first; this is the subsequent explicit per-word first-author pass. Spec independent pass was already complete; its detailed artifact/conclusions were not consulted. Original research/proposal and first-author provenance files remain unchanged.
keyFormat: Each identity is the tuple lemma, word, recordSha256 (source row raw hash), senseIndex (zero-based within source row). Same spelling under different roots or senses remains distinct.

guards: Approval binds unchanged selected template and context, not every root sense or all uses of the spelling.
Only explicit source single accusative lo/la/los/las: singular it or plural them, selected inanimate reading. Spanish grammatical gender retained without invented English nouns.

Infinitives keep subject unspecified. Imperative third-person grammar is usted/ustedes addressee, never a he/she declarative. Explicit second-person voseo labels retained for SABELA, ACABALA and ACABALO.
No suffix decomposition, table-only authority, finite indicative, negative imperative, dative, se/reflexive, multiple-clitic or lexical fixed-clitic idiom authority.
Keep object in explicitly reviewed English particle slot: turn it on, take it out, fill it up; no invented location or recipient.

Keep lexical selected-sense qualifications, including cooking-with-heat COCER, wine CATAR, preserve-food CURAR, Canary Islands/Latin America BOTAR, and COGER warning about its separate Mexican vulgar sexual uses. Do not mislabel unrelated root-sense warnings as this selected sense.
Same-spelling CRÉALA/CRÉALO source CREAR informal commands and CREER formal commands remain separately bound; CRÉELO CREAR formal and CREER informal readings are likewise distinct.
These are selected grammatical English readings, not complete example sentences, universal translations, new answer eligibility or measured coverage.
